target_customer: Originally small and medium businesses in Singapore running payroll; today engineering teams that want to run background coding agents
problem: Original: payroll in Southeast Asia was manual, spread across spreadsheets and outsourced providers, with costly compliance and cross-border payments. Current: teams lack a ready platform for collaborative background agents.
business_model: Originally B2B SaaS payroll with compliance service; now an open source project (monetization not stated)
product_category: payroll software, later open source AI background agents platform

founders.name: Jonathan Low
previous_startups: Honestbee (co-founded 2015, grocery delivery in Southeast Asia; Honestbee later cut staff and wound down, per TechCrunch 2019 layoffs article only noted)
founders.background_notes: YC page: led product development and digital transformation at NTUC Enterprise; co-founded Honestbee from 2015 to 2019.

founders.name: Thomas Jiang
prior_employers: B2B enterprise compliance software startup (acquired), engineer number 2
founders.background_notes: YC page and launch post; launch post says he saw SMB owners run payroll on spreadsheets.

founders.name: Cayter Goh
founders.background_notes: YC page: VP Engineering at Spenmo, engineering lead at Rapyd APAC and Grab SEA; launch post says wide exposure to payments.

competitors.name: Vara
competitors.what: Attendance and payroll software for small businesses in Singapore

competitors.name: StaffAny
competitors.what: Singapore shift management and workforce tool for SMEs
competitors.funding_then: US$3.4M led by GGV in January 2022

competitors.name: Omni HR
competitors.what: HR automation platform for Southeast Asia covering onboarding, leave and documents
competitors.funding_then: US$2.4M pre-seed in July 2022 led by Alpha JWC and Picus Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll needs statutory filings, bank disbursement integrations and compliance accuracy, which is standard engineering with hard regulatory edges for a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll has some switching costs once data and filings are set up, but no proprietary data or network effect was shown and local HR rivals were funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the payroll product; the company later moved to a different product.

market_need_then: The YC launch post says payroll in Southeast Asia was handled on spreadsheets or outsourced, and funding rounds into Singapore SME HR tools in 2021 and 2022 show investor interest. Omni HR's 2022 release says local HR tools covered only basic admin.

branding.domain_note: Current site is mistle.dev, a .dev domain; the original YC listing used the Ajourney launch name, with the YC S22 company page now carrying the Mistle name.

identity.logo: A Mistle logo image appears in directories but no source describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct developer tone: the open source alternative to Stripe Minions, Ramp Inspect and Shopify River

branding.brand_signature: The line open source background agents

rebrands.why: Not stated by a source; the YC launch post for Ajourney lists the company as Mistle with a link to mistle.dev

branding.community_and_virality: A Show HN post on May 13, 2026 for the repo (37 GitHub stars at the time of the snippet); a community Slack is linked from the site.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community beyond a small Show HN; the name was changed after the original product, so there was no brand equity from the YC period.

pivots.from: Ajourney, payroll platform for Southeast Asia (Gusto for SEA)
pivots.why: Not stated by any source; inferred only from the launch page and site naming. Timing rests on a May 2026 Show HN.

outcome_analysis: The company entered YC Summer 2022 as Ajourney, a payroll product for Singapore SMEs, and the cause of its inactive status is not public. Public funding data is thin: one database shows a 2024 accelerator entry from AppWorks and YC and a total near 500 thousand dollars. By 2026 the founders were building an open source background agents project under the Mistle name, which suggests the payroll product did not become a venture scale business, but no source says so. Failure factors are tentative.
notes: The YC company page now describes Mistle (2026 product) while the S22 launch was Ajourney, payroll. The batch competitors above are for the payroll product, as of 2022-08. Funding: the 2024-06 entry rests on a single database family (CB Insights and VCBacked, labeled incubator or non-equity assistance, amount undisclosed; CB Insights total about 500K over 2 rounds); a Seedtable pre-seed entry dated 2022-10 for a company called journey could not be opened (403) and is unverified. The failure factor is a tentative reading. The pivot date and Honestbee outcome are not confirmed by an opened source on the outcome.
